newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: BANK PRIVATISATION LEAD ADVISOR TO BE PICKED.
newsitem.headline: BANK PRIVATISATION LEAD ADVISOR TO BE PICKED.

text.p: Lithuanian Finance Minister Algirdas Shemeta said on Thursday that the process of finding a lead advisor for the sale of the state-run State Commercial Bank should be finished today.
"Concerning the lead advisor for the privatisation of the State Commercial Bank, the selection process should be completed today," Shemeta told Reuters at a conference on capital markets here.
"The tentative plan is to then launch a tender during the last ten days of May (for the actual privatisation)...and the results should be known by the start of July," he said.
The State Commercial Bank is one of two state-run banks which have been slated for privatisation in Lithuania.
The bank suffered a staggering loss of over 170 million litas in 1996 and was rescued by the government to the tune of 165 million litas in fresh share capital.
But its huge branch network alone makes it look relatively attractive to potential investors, analysts say.
